newsitem.title: USA: United Space names Smith CEO.
newsitem.headline: United Space names Smith CEO.

text.p: United Space Alliance, a joint venture between Boeing Co and Lockheed Martin Corp, said on Wednesday that it has named Paul Smith president and chief executive officer, effective April 1, 1997.
Smith, president of Boeing North American's Rocketdyne Division, is replacing Kent Black, United Space Alliance said.
Black is retiring as chief executive after a combined 34 years with Rockwell International Corp and the venture, United Space Alliance said.
Rockwell was an original partner in the United Space Alliance, but Boeing acquired Rockwell's space and defense operations in a deal that closed in December 1996, the company said.
Black was the first chief executive of United Space and he played a key role in completing the terms of the venture's space flight operations contract with NASA, United Space said.
United Space president Denton Hanford will return to Boeing and aid in the merger plans between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp, the venture said.
